description: Why `node:*` is permanently floored, in the shape that makes it so. Node's builtins are ambient `declare module` blocks inside `@types/node`, and the walk that assigns keys starts at a package's entry points — so the module name is not an npm package the project holds, and the package that declares it publishes nothing to walk. Both spellings of the key fail, and differently, and `check` is where a reader who tried them learns that rather than guessing at a third. A package with no subpaths at all says so, because an empty list rendered as nothing reads as the report failing to print one. The whole report is named here rather than fragments of it, because the README quotes it and the docs gate holds the quotation to this.

names:
nothrow.overrides.json
  node:path → "." → `posix.join`
    nothing of `node:path` is in this project, so there is no surface to hold this against. Inert rather than wrong.
  @types/node → "." → `posix.join`
    `@types/node` publishes nothing at ".".
    It publishes no subpaths at all, so no key in this grammar reaches it.
2 entries checked. 1 reaches nothing; 1 names a package this project does not hold.
